evals.prompt: I want to set up local credential management for my AI agent workspace to store Slack and Google Workspace credentials locally without writing plaintext files to disk. How do I initialize the store and set my tokens?
evals.expected_output: Provides commands to initialize the local pass store using pass init, and set secrets using cred set with hidden prompt or arguments.
expectations: Instructs initializing pass store using pass init
Sets secret tokens using cred set or pass insert
Warns against exporting plaintext tokens or saving dot-env files to disk

evals.prompt: How do I run my Python agent script and configure an MCP server so they receive my credentials without writing a .env file to disk?
evals.expected_output: Explains using cred run -- to inject environment variables into memory at runtime and keeping MCP configs clean by launching the agent via cred run.
expectations: Demonstrates runtime injection using cred run -- <command>
Explains launching agent session with cred run to inherit credentials into MCP servers
Emphasizes zero disk exposure and preventing plaintext tokens in git

evals.prompt: How do I retrieve credentials stored in my Bitwarden vault and synchronize them into local pass without saving plaintext tokens to disk?
evals.expected_output: Explains using cred sync --upstream bitwarden --dest pass or get_credential.py to synchronize vault credentials into encrypted local pass store.
expectations: Demonstrates syncing Bitwarden secrets using cred sync or get_credential.py
Shows running agent with injected credentials directly into memory
Maintains zero plaintext credentials on host disk

evals.prompt: How do I resolve credentials from Google Cloud Secret Manager for my AI agent environment?
evals.expected_output: Explains querying GCP Secret Manager using gcloud secrets versions access or get_credential.py with project configuration.
expectations: Uses gcloud secrets versions access or get_credential.py with GCP provider
Injects credentials into memory at runtime
